title: Rate Charged for Each Chargeable Mile as a Car Rental Overage Grows
content:
The rate charged for each chargeable mile on a rental of the Car Rental Rate Classes falls as the overage grows. The included allowance standing on the rental is the miles the mileage grants on its ledger have placed on it, added together; the chargeable miles are the miles driven beyond that allowance less the miles carried free on the rental, and they never fall below nothing.

**The rate schedule.**

| The chargeable miles stand at | The rate for each chargeable mile |
|---|---|
| 500 miles or more | 0.20 |
| 150 miles or more, but below 500 | 0.26 |
| Below 150 miles | The rate class's own excess rate per mile |

**Both sides of each threshold.** At exactly 500 chargeable miles the rate is 0.20; at 499 it is 0.26. At exactly 150 chargeable miles the rate is 0.26; at 149 it is the excess rate published for the class booked. At no chargeable mile at all, nothing is charged whatever rate would apply.

**Illustration on hypothetical figures.** A rental whose allowance stands at 600 miles, on which 1400 miles were driven and 60 miles are carried free, has 740 chargeable miles and is charged at 0.20 for each of them. A rental with 220 chargeable miles is charged at 0.26 for each. A rental with 90 chargeable miles is charged at the excess rate published for its own class.
